headline: Delegation Escalation is the biggest risk in enterprise AI, not prompt injection
summary: Enterprise AI's biggest architectural risk is Delegation Escalation, a "Confused Deputy" vulnerability. Secure multi-agent chains require OAuth 2.1 RFC 8693 Token Exchange with explicit actor claims.
details: The biggest architectural risk in enterprise AI isn't prompt injection, but "Delegation Escalation." This occurs when an AI Agent Orchestrator delegates tasks to sub-agents, creating a "Confused Deputy" vulnerability if broad bearer tokens or static user API keys are passed down.

To safely deploy autonomous multi-agent chains at enterprise scale, platform architects must enforce OAuth 2.1 RFC 8693 Token Exchange. This ensures every issued JWT token contains a nested actor claim, verifying both the human authorizer and the executing agent.

One non-negotiable rule is "Delegation Over Impersonation" (RFC 8693). Agents should never blindly impersonate a user; downstream APIs must verify who authorized the action and which agent executed it via nested actor claims.

Another key principle is the "Intersection of Privileges (User 
 Agent)." An agent's runtime authority must be the strict mathematical intersection of the user's IAM permissions and the agent's registered tool scope. Agents should never acquire more system access than the human user who invoked them.

Finally, "Ephemeral Tokens & DPoP Binding" (RFC 9449) is crucial. Static API keys and long-lived refresh tokens should be eliminated in favor of short-lived tokens (5-minute TTL) cryptographically bound via DPoP or mTLS to prevent replay attacks.

Treating AI agents as traditional service accounts is a mistake, as non-human identities vastly outnumber human users in modern cloud environments. Without proper auditing of nested delegation chains, agentic architectures pose a significant unmonitored security breach risk.

headline_marked: [[Financial document OCR with Claude Vision API]] sees 94% accuracy, 5x cost cut
headline: Financial document OCR with Claude Vision API sees 94% accuracy, 5x cost cut
summary: Lessons from processing thousands of financial documents with Claude Vision API reveal how to achieve 94% accuracy and reduce costs by 5x, overcoming common OCR challenges.
details: Financial document OCR is complex, with traditional tools struggling to parse raw text into structured data. Claude Vision API offers a solution by understanding document structure directly.

Instead of raw text, Claude Vision can extract structured JSON from images with a simple prompt, eliminating the need for extensive regex or manual column detection. This streamlines data processing significantly.

A key challenge is poor image quality from phone photos. Preprocessing techniques, including deskewing, binarization, and noise reduction, boosted accuracy on mobile-captured statements from 78% to 94%.

For multi-page documents, processing only the first and last pages for most use cases, and batch-processing middle pages when full history is needed, reduced costs by 5x, from $0.15 to $0.03 per statement.

Despite its advantages, Claude occasionally misreads numbers (e.g., 1,234.56 as 123456) and Sonnet 4 can hit rate limits. For these specific cases, alternatives like AWS Textract with custom parsing or on-premise OCR might be considered.

Current costs are $0.03 per bank statement and $0.01 per receipt using this optimized setup. A free tool, CleanStmt, is available to test Claude Vision's capabilities for converting bank statements to Excel/CSV.
